topic: Research: Computer Use Agents Compared: Claude vs Codex vs Gemini for Developers

key_points: OpenAI introduced Codex as a cloud-based software-engineering agent that can handle features, bug fixes, and PR-style workflows in isolated environments.
Codex completion time was described as 1–30 minutes depending on task complexity and provides verifiable logs and test outputs before users approve final changes.
Codex usage is plan-based and counts toward an aggregate agentic usage limit for ChatGPT plans.
Compliance API, memories, automations, browser access, and computer use are all listed as key feature buckets in the Codex usage guidance.
April 2026 rollout brought broader Codex workflows beyond coding, including context-aware memory, project review, and stronger computer-use coverage on macOS first.
The update explicitly frames Codex as a broader software workflow layer across planning, understanding, and task continuity.
Gemini CLI is launched as an open-source terminal agent with MCP/extension support and integration with Gemini Code Assist in VS Code.
Google highlights a large free tier (60 RPM / 1,000 requests per day) and 1M token context window in the initial announcement.
Claude Code is positioned as an agent for full codebase navigation, CI monitoring, dependency tracing, and autonomous file edits with PR-level outcomes.
The product page shares concrete deployment examples (e.g., large migrations) and notes safety controls (human-in-the-loop approval, explicit permission model).
Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 add stronger agentic behavior, tool parallelism, and long-context coding capabilities.
Anthropic reports high benchmark performance (SWE-bench 72.5% and Terminal-bench 43.2%) in this release update.

stats.fact: CCBench 2026 results show Codex CLI with GPT 5.2-codex at 75.4% success vs Claude Code with Opus 4.6 at 72.7% and Gemini CLI with Gemini 3 Flash at 51.3%.
Gemini CLI announcement states a free allowance of 60 model requests per minute and 1,000 requests per day with a personal Google account.
Claude Opus 4 is reported to lead on SWE-bench (72.5%) and terminal-bench (43.2%) in Anthropic’s 2026 model update.
OpenAI API changelog notes GPT-5.2-codex optimized for agentic coding in Codex and ~40% faster inference in February 2026.
GitHub ecosystem signals: openai/codex shows around 90.3k stars and 13.3k forks (while the task snapshot was fetched), while google-gemini/gemini-cli shows about 105k stars and 14k forks.

angles: The 2026 shift is from "coding assistant" to computer-native workflow agent: Codex and Claude both market end-to-end context and multi-step execution, while Gemini CLI emphasizes terminal-first extensibility.
Benchmarking is becoming more nuanced: SWE-bench alone underestimates real-world task diversity, so CCBench-style smaller-codebase metrics materially change comparisons.
Open-source surface area is now a competitive factor: Gemini CLI’s free/open distribution plus release velocity can matter more for engineering teams than raw headline scores.
Governance and safety posture differ: Anthropic leans explicit approvals and classifier-backed prompt-injection mitigation, while Codex emphasizes RBAC, compliance logging, and workspace controls.
Feature velocity appears highest in 2026-era updates (model optimization, platform channels, desktop/workspace expansions), so comparisons need explicit update freshness windows.
